headline: Google commits €13B ($15.1B) to Finland AI infrastructure with 22-year Loviisa nuclear PPA - first ex-US Google nuclear contract
summary: Google announced its single largest European investment: at least €13B ($15.1B) into AI-optimized datacenters in Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala across 2027-2028. Anchor deal is a 22-year life-extension PPA with Fortum's 1,020 MW Loviisa nuclear plant - Google's first nuclear contract outside the US and the extension that keeps Loviisa (10% of Finnish power) operating past 2030. Bundled with 629 MW of new onshore wind PPAs (Valorem, Suomen Hyotytuuli) and a 94 MW battery at Kajaani. Construction phase estimated to add ~€3.6B/yr to Finnish GDP and support 37,000 jobs.

headline: Barclays cuts US utilities sector (XLU) to Neutral from Positive, citing crowded positioning after 2026 outperformance
summary: Barclays' equity strategy team downgraded the S&P Utilities sector rating to Neutral from Positive Wednesday, arguing valuations have caught up after utilities rerated on AI-power tailwinds. The call directly impacts nuclear-levered independent power producers (VST, CEG) and rate-regulated AI-power beneficiaries (NEE, AES). Barclays also lifted its S&P 500 year-end target to 7,950 from 7,800 - a defensive rotation call rather than a broad de-risking. Utility ETF XLU indicated -1% pre-market.

headline: Vistra files mixed shelf offering for common and preferred stock; size undisclosed
summary: Vistra Corp. filed an automatic mixed shelf covering common stock and preferred stock with no dollar amount specified, giving the company flexibility to raise equity capital opportunistically. Shelf follows a year of aggressive nuclear/gas capacity buildouts (Meta PPA >2,600 MW, corporate power deals) and comes as VST trades below its 200-day MA. Filing coincided with the Barclays utilities-sector downgrade - shelf overhang could pressure shares in the near term though management retains discretion to activate.

headline: US 10Y yield hits 4.82%, highest since 2023; Brent crude tops $99 on Iran tanker strikes; rate-sensitive AI-infra names on watch
summary: Treasury yields extended the Labor Day back-up, with the 10Y printing 4.82% intraday - the highest level since October 2023 - as the market digests strong August payrolls and awaits Friday's CPI (consensus 3.4% headline). Brent crude spiked toward $100/bbl after US strikes on five Iranian tankers near Kharg Island; Tehran retaliated with ballistic missiles toward Jordan and threats to Persian Gulf shipping. Nasdaq 100 futures -0.47%, S&P 500 futures -0.32%. Long-duration AI plays (OKLO, SMR, PLTR, SNOW) and hyperscaler capex names most exposed to duration and energy-cost pass-through.

headline: Oracle Q1 FY27 preview: Street $19.13B rev / $1.30 EPS Thursday post-close; RPO conversion and OCI cadence are the print
summary: Oracle reports fiscal Q1 2027 after the close Thursday Sept 10 (not Wednesday - some outlets initially miscalendared). Consensus: $19.13B revenue (+~28% YoY), $1.30 EPS (+18%). Focus: OCI growth vs. management's >92% FY27 guide, conversion cadence on record $638B RPO, and any color on debt issuance funding the buildout. Guggenheim called ORCL its 'best idea' at $400 PT; options price ~11% post-print move. Polymarket implies 83.5% odds of a beat.

headline: Apple 'Surprise and Shine' iPhone 18 Pro / iPhone Ultra foldable event today at 1pm ET - first event under CEO John Ternus
summary: Apple's fall product event kicks off 10am PT / 1pm ET today from Apple Park. First event helmed by new CEO John Ternus (took over Sept 1). Expected: iPhone 18 Pro / Pro Max, foldable 'iPhone Ultra', Watch Series 12 (ceramic option), two AirPods 5 SKUs. Standard iPhone 18 held for spring 2027. Read-through for tracked names: TSMC (A20 Pro node), SK Hynix / Samsung / Micron (mobile DRAM - the same HBM4-wafer-diversion narrative from this week's KB note applies), Broadcom (5G/WiFi silicon), Amphenol (interconnect).

headline: NuScale +13%, Oklo +7% Tuesday on nuclear-sector short-covering with no company catalyst - options positioning drove the pop
summary: Tuesday Sept 8 saw NuScale (SMR) jump 13% and Oklo (OKLO) climb 7% on a broad SMR rotation with URA uranium ETF up 4%. Neither company issued fresh news - move was short-covering into thin books carrying big options gamma (SMR put/call 0.20, OKLO 0.29). Structural: NuScale is still the only NRC design-certified SMR (ENTRA1/TVA discussions ongoing); Oklo carries a ~14 GW pipeline (Switch 12 GW, Equinix 500 MW LOI with $25M prepayment). Both remain deeply negative YTD (SMR -24%, OKLO -39%) and remain at elevated duration risk into next week's FOMC.

headline: Qualcomm upgraded to Strong Buy at CFRA on Snapdragon AI PC momentum and edge-inference share; QCOM read-through for MediaTek and Arm
summary: CFRA lifted Qualcomm to Strong Buy Wednesday citing accelerating Snapdragon X and X2 AI-PC design wins, edge-inference share gains, and improving auto SoC visibility. QCOM is not a house-tracked ticker but the call is read-across for the on-device AI theme (marginal negative for datacenter GPU/ASIC demand at the low end, marginal positive for memory bit-shipment demand). Coincides with today's Apple event which will showcase competing Apple Silicon inference.

headline: Fortum-Google Loviisa PPA validates Big Tech buying European nuclear extensions - precedent for CEG, EDF, ENGIE playbook
summary: Beyond the headline $ figure, the structural signal from Google's Fortum deal is that hyperscalers are willing to underwrite European reactor life-extensions the way Amazon (Talen), Meta (Constellation, Vistra) and Microsoft (Constellation Crane restart) have done in the US. Fortum-Loviisa keeps 1,020 MW online past 2030. Constructive read-through for CEG in the US (still the deepest existing-fleet portfolio), plus signal to EU utilities (Fortum, EDF, ENGIE, Iberdrola) that AI-driven PPAs unlock capex that ratepayer economics alone could not.

headline: Galaxy Digital secures 4.2 GW of conditional ERCOT classifications across five Texas datacenter projects
summary: Galaxy Digital (GLXY) received conditional ERCOT classifications on five Texas datacenter projects totaling ~4.2 GW of connection capacity. ERCOT classification is a critical early step in the Texas interconnection queue - conditional status locks a queue position while transmission studies advance. Signal: Texas is absorbing significant hyperscaler-adjacent capacity outside of ERCOT's most congested nodes; read-through to VRT (grid-to-building interconnect exposure announced this week) and GEV/Siemens Energy (gas turbine off-take for baseload).
